Fact.Name: Schedule C businesses
Fact.Description: One or more sole-proprietor / gig businesses reported on Schedule C. Gross income inclusion authority: 26 U.S.C. § 61.

Fact.Name: Schedule C businesses done
Fact.Description: Filer finished the Schedule C business loop.

Fact.Name: Has Schedule C businesses
Fact.Description: Whether any Schedule C businesses are listed.

Fact.Name: A Schedule C business still uses the single expense total
Fact.Description: True when any Schedule C business still uses the pre-line-item expense total (/scheduleCBusinesses/*/usesLegacyExpenseBucket). False when there is no Schedule C, and when every business is on the line-item path. A mixed return stays true: PA-40 line 4 is one sum, so a business that cannot be mapped onto PA Schedule C keeps /flowKnockoutPaScheduleC true. The count is not read when there is no Schedule C, so a W-2-only return stays complete.

Fact.Name: More than one business uses the simplified method
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 12: "You are limited to a maximum of 300 square feet for all of the businesses you conduct in your home." This tool does not split that maximum. More than one business that elects the simplified method stops the return. A business that has not started the line-item questions, that does not claim a home office, or that does not elect the simplified method is not counted. An unanswered election on a started line-item business stays incomplete. Rev. Proc. 2013-13.

Fact.Name: A line-item Schedule C business claims business use of the home
Fact.Description: True when any started line-item business answers yes to business use of the home. Pennsylvania does not recognize the federal safe harbor, and PA Schedule C-2 actual expenses are not computed. PA-40 C (EX) 03-26 instructions, PDF p. 4: "Pennsylvania does not recognize the federal safe harbor method." A business that still uses the single expense total is not counted; that return is already stopped by /scheduleCHasLegacyExpenseBucket. False when there is no Schedule C. Read by /flowKnockoutPaScheduleC.

Fact.Name: Had self-employment / gig / freelance income
Fact.Description: Interview gate: whether the filer (or spouse) had self-employment, gig, or freelance income that belongs on Schedule C. Gap evidence Pub 6048 excluded this from upstream Direct File: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p6048.pdf

Fact.Name: Wants qualified business income deduction (no longer asked)
Fact.Description: Kept so saved returns still load. The 26 U.S.C. 199A(a) deduction is not elective (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A), and Form 8995 (form8995.xml, #87) now computes it, so this answer is not used anywhere.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule C QBI deduction case Form 8995 here can't compute
Fact.Description: #87: Schedule C qualified business income is computed on Form 8995 (form8995.xml). This is true when the return has Schedule C qualified business income and any Form 8995 stop applies: a prior-year loss carryforward, a cooperative patron, active and non-active trades together, or taxable income before the deduction above the threshold (Form 8995-A). A section 162 rental with no Schedule C does not make this true. A 1099-DIV box 5 return with no Schedule C income does not make this true either; that return stops on the Form 8995 facts (/flowKnockoutQbiAboveThreshold, /flowKnockoutQbiPriorYearCarryforward) (#186). Each part is its own BlockSubmissionOnTrue fact in /flowIsKnockedOut. Used for the Schedule C knockout screen.

Fact.Name: Schedule C businesses owned by the secondary filer
Secondary filer's Schedule C net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: #118. Sum of /scheduleCBusinesses/*/netProfitOrLoss for the businesses the secondary filer owns: the line 3 of that spouse's own Schedule SE. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 3: "If both spouses have self-employment income, each must file a separate Schedule SE." $0 on a return that isn't a joint return (only a joint return reports a spouse's business) or when the filer answered no to self-employment income; incomplete while businesses are still being entered, like /scheduleCNetProfitOrLoss.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Schedule C net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: #118. Every business not owned by the secondary filer is the primary filer's (/scheduleCBusinesses/*/filer defaults to the primary filer), so this is /scheduleCNetProfitOrLoss minus /scheduleCSecondaryFilerNetProfitOrLoss, and the two always add up to Schedule 1 line 3.

Fact.Name: Schedule C gross nonfarm income
Fact.Description: Sum of Schedule C line 7 for every business. 2026 draft Schedule SE Part II uses this as gross nonfarm income for the nonfarm optional method. Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code C is not collected. On the single expense-total path, lines 2, 4, and 6 are zero, so line 7 equals gross receipts. Complete the same way as /scheduleCNetProfitOrLoss.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's Schedule C gross nonfarm income
Fact.Description: Sum of Schedule C line 7 for businesses the secondary filer owns. $0 when the return is not a joint return. Used for that spouse's Schedule SE Part II nonfarm optional method.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Schedule C gross nonfarm income
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 7 for the primary filer: /scheduleCGrossNonfarmIncome minus /scheduleCSecondaryFilerGrossNonfarmIncome. The two add up to every business's line 7.

Fact.Name: Knockout: spouse-owned Schedule C business
Fact.Description: Schedule SE is figured per filer (scheduleSE /secondaryFilerSelfEmploymentTax, with that spouse's own OASDI base under 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1)) and Schedule 2 line 4, Schedule 1 line 15 and Form 8959 line 13 combine both. A secondary filer's business still stops the return until the rest of that spouse's path is per spouse: EITC and CDCC earned income with self-employment (Form 2441 lines 4 and 5 are per spouse), and the printed return has no Schedule SE form yet (one per spouse once it does).

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule C cases the EITC, CDCC or ACTC earned income can't yet figure
Fact.Description: #117. The EITC (eitc /eitcEarnedIncomeWithoutCombatPay), the CDCC (income /primaryFilerEarnedIncomeForCdccBase) and the ACTC (income /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay) add /scheduleCNetProfitForEarnedIncome. Still stopped: - A Schedule C net loss. Both sources say a loss reduces earned income: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), PDF p. 47, EIC Worksheet B, line 1e and line 4b ("Combine lines 1e, 2c, 3, and 4a"), and the 2026 draft Instructions for Form 2441, PDF p. 5 ("You must reduce your earned income by any loss from self-employment"). /scheduleCNetProfitForEarnedIncome is floored at $0, so a loss stops the return when the EITC could apply (AGI below the EITC completed phaseout, eitc /belowEitcAgiLimit, or eitc /eitcQualified), the CDCC applies or the CTC applies. A loss can lower earned income below the EITC limit even when wages alone are above it, so the EITC test is on AGI, which already includes the loss. - A joint return with any Schedule C result and the CDCC: Form 2441 lines 4 and 5 need each spouse's Schedule SE line 3 and Schedule 1 line 15 share ("If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately"), and Schedule SE is not yet figured per spouse. Stopped elsewhere: a spouse-owned business (/flowKnockoutScheduleCSpouseBusiness), statutory employees (formW2s /flowKnockoutStatutoryEmployee), and farm income, the farm optional method, church employee income, ministry or Forms 4361 and 4029, notary fees, and Form 8919 wages (scheduleSE /flowKnockoutScheduleSEOutOfScope). The nonfarm optional method is figured on Schedule SE unless the election fails the dollar or prior-year tests (scheduleSE /flowKnockoutScheduleSENonfarmOptionalMethod). An election that applies together with the earned income credit, the additional child tax credit, or the child and dependent care credit stops on /flowKnockoutScheduleSENonfarmOptionalMethodCredits, which is not part of /scheduleCSectionIsComplete. Line 4b is not added to this earned-income amount. Complete and false when there is no Schedule C or the Schedule C result is a profit on a return that isn't a joint return claiming the CDCC.

Fact.Name: Business owner (filer)
Fact.Description: Which filer owns this Schedule C business.

Fact.Name: Business name
Fact.Description: Schedule C line C, "Business name. If no separate business name, leave blank." 2026 Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sc.pdf), PDF p. 1. This is not line A.

Fact.Name: Principal business or profession
Fact.Description: Schedule C line A, the general field of the activity. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 4, Line A: "Describe the business or professional activity that provided your principal source of income reported on line 1," including "the general field or activity and the type of product or service."

Fact.Name: Principal product or service
Fact.Description: The product or service included in Schedule C line A. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 4, Line A. PA-40 C (EX) 03-26 prints this in its own box beside "Main business activity."

Fact.Name: Schedule C line A
Fact.Description: Line A text: the activity and the product or service. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 4, Line A, "including product or service." Incomplete until both parts are answered.

Fact.Name: Principal business code
Fact.Description: Schedule C line B. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 4, Line B: "Enter on line B the six-digit code from the Principal Business or Professional Activity Codes chart at the end of these instructions." The allowed set is that chart (draft PDF pp. 19-20). A six-digit code that is not on the chart is rejected. The same code is the Federal NAICS Code on PA-40 C (EX) 03-26.

Fact.Name: Business has an EIN
Fact.Description: Schedule C line D. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 4, Line D: enter the EIN from Form SS-4; do not enter an SSN; if you do not have an EIN, leave line D blank. PA-40 C (EX) 03-26: if the business has no FEIN, leave the EIN blank. Yes asks for the EIN. No prints a blank line D. Unanswered stays incomplete.

Fact.Name: Employer identification number
Fact.Description: The EIN for Schedule C line D and PA-40 C. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 4, Line D. Not the filer's SSN, and not another person's EIN.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line D
Fact.Description: The EIN text when the filer has one. A complete "no" is a blank line D. Unanswered stays incomplete. Yes without an EIN stays incomplete and prints blank; it is not treated as "no EIN." 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 4, Line D.

Fact.Name: Business is conducted at the home address on the return
Fact.Description: Schedule C line E. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 5, Line E: if you conducted the business from your home at the address shown on page 1 of the return, you do not have to complete line E. Yes leaves federal line E blank. PA-40 C (EX) 03-26 still asks for the complete business address, which is then the address on the return. No asks for a separate business address.

Fact.Name: Ask for a separate business address
Fact.Description: True only after the filer says the business is not at the address on the return. Unanswered is false, so the address screen stays hidden and line E is not copied from the home address.

Fact.Name: Business address
Fact.Description: Schedule C line E when the business is not conducted at the address on page 1 of the return. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 5, Line E: street address, not a box number, and the suite or room number if any. Also the PA-40 C business address in that case.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line E street
Fact.Description: Blank when the business is at the address on the return. Otherwise the business street. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 5, Line E.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line E apartment
Fact.Description: Line E suite, room, or apartment. Blank when the business is at the address on the return, or when the separate address has no second line. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 5, Line E.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line E city
Fact.Description: Line E city. Blank when the business is at the address on the return. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 5, Line E.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line E state
Fact.Description: Line E state. Blank when the business is at the address on the return. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 5, Line E.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line E ZIP code
Fact.Description: Line E ZIP code. Blank when the business is at the address on the return. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 5, Line E.

Fact.Name: Schedule C accounting methods
Fact.Description: Schedule C line F: cash, accrual, or other. 26 U.S.C. 446(c) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/446). 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 5, Line F. Cash and accrual print. Other stops the return. This tool does not file Form 3115 or figure a section 481(a) adjustment.

Fact.Name: Accounting method
Fact.Description: Schedule C line F and PA-40 C accounting method. 26 U.S.C. 446(c). 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 5, Line F. Unanswered is not treated as cash. Other is a form stop.

Fact.Name: Line F cash
Fact.Description: Complete false until an accounting method is chosen. True only for cash. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 1, line F (1).

Fact.Name: Line F accrual
Fact.Description: Complete false until an accounting method is chosen. True only for accrual. 26 U.S.C. 446(c)(2). 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 1, line F (2).

Fact.Name: Line F other
Fact.Description: Complete false until an accounting method is chosen. True only for other. That answer is a form stop: line F (3) and the specify line are not printed, and Form 3115 is not filed. 26 U.S.C. 446(c)(3). 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 5, Line F. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 1, line F (3).

Fact.Name: Started or acquired this business in 2026
Fact.Description: Schedule C line H. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf, SHA-256 27a6e185504f442c363b2d659a33cfc61613b669025cb2bd3de2ec81599009f9), PDF p. 6, Line H: "If you started or acquired this business in 2026, check the box on line H. Also, check the box if you are reopening or restarting this business after temporarily closing it, and you didn’t file a 2025 Schedule C for this business." Required. Incomplete until answered. There is no default of no. Does not change net profit.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line H checkbox
Fact.Description: Complete true only after the filer answers yes. Complete false when the answer is no or still missing, so the box is not checked and an unanswered line is not treated as no. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 1, line H (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sc.pdf, SHA-256 cc44e7d1150e54d991835814c1191f60a32617730ca9e50e6f532b51293a86b4): "If you started or acquired this business during 2026, check here."

Fact.Name: Made a payment that requires Form 1099
Fact.Description: Schedule C line I. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf, SHA-256 27a6e185504f442c363b2d659a33cfc61613b669025cb2bd3de2ec81599009f9), PDF p. 6, Line I: "If you made any payment in 2026 that would require you to file any Forms 1099, check the “Yes” box. Otherwise, check the “No” box." "For 2026, the information reporting threshold for certain payments reported on Forms 1099 increased from $600 to $2,000." 26 U.S.C. 6041(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6041), as amended by P.L. 119-21. Required. Incomplete until answered. There is no default of no. Does not change net profit.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line I Yes
Fact.Description: Complete true only after line I is answered yes. Otherwise complete false, so neither the Yes box nor a default No is printed while the question is unanswered. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 6, Line I.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line I No
Fact.Description: Complete true only after line I is answered no. Complete false while line I is unanswered, so the No box is not a default. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 6, Line I: "Otherwise, check the “No” box."

Fact.Name: Will file required Forms 1099
Fact.Description: Schedule C line J, asked only when line I is yes. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 1, line J (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sc.pdf, SHA-256 cc44e7d1150e54d991835814c1191f60a32617730ca9e50e6f532b51293a86b4): "If “Yes,” did you or will you file required Form(s) 1099?" Required after line I is yes. Incomplete until answered. There is no default of no. When line I is no, this answer is not used. Does not change net profit.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line J Yes
Fact.Description: Complete true only when line I is yes and line J is answered yes. Complete false when line I is no, when line I is unanswered, or when line J is unanswered, so line J is not printed in those cases. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 1, line J.

Fact.Name: Schedule C line J No
Fact.Description: Complete true only when line I is yes and line J is answered no. Complete false when line I is no, so line J is not printed. Also complete false while line J is unanswered, so No is not a default. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 1, line J: "If “Yes,” did you or will you file required Form(s) 1099?"

Fact.Name: Schedule C header lines A through J are answered
Fact.Description: Activity, product or service, a code on the chart, EIN yes or no, home-address yes or no, accounting method, line H, and line I. An EIN is required only after yes. A separate address is required only after no. Line J is required only after line I is yes. When line I is no, line J is complete false and is not printed. Other is a complete answer and a form stop; it is not printed. Missing answers are not defaulted. Lines H, I, and J do not change net profit. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 4, PDF p. 5, and PDF p. 6. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 1, line J.

Fact.Name: Gross receipts or sales
Fact.Description: Schedule C Part I gross receipts (cash MVP). Inclusion: 26 U.S.C. § 61. Cite Schedule C instructions PDF page for the line rule used in the implementation PR notes.

Fact.Name: Gross receipts or sales (derived)
Fact.Description: Gross receipts defaulting incomplete writable to zero for sums.

Fact.Name: Total business expenses (MVP)
Fact.Description: MVP expense bucket (sum of deductible trade/business expenses). Authority: 26 U.S.C. § 162 (ordinary and necessary expenses paid or incurred in carrying on a trade or business) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/162 Kept for a return that already stored one total. The interview now asks the Schedule C lines. Once any line-item answer is complete, this total is ignored.

Fact.Name: Total business expenses (derived)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 28. On a return that only stored one expense total, that total. On the line-item path, the sum of the supported lines, and only when no out-of-scope form applies. Otherwise incomplete: an unanswered expense is not treated as zero. 26 U.S.C. 162(a).

Fact.Name: Net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 31. 2026 Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sc.pdf), line 31: subtract line 30 from line 29. Single-total path: line 29, which is gross receipts minus that total, and line 30 is zero. Line-item path: line 29 minus line 30, and only when both are complete and no out-of-scope form applies. A loss that needs Form 6198 or Form 8582 is still computed and is stopped by /flowKnockoutScheduleCOutOfScope, because the stop reads this result and this result must not read the stop. 26 U.S.C. 61, 162, 280A(c)(5), 465, 469.

Fact.Name: Schedule C business complete
Fact.Description: Single-total path: header lines A through F and H, I, and J, name, gross receipts, the expense total, and material participation. Line-item path: header lines A through F and H, I, and J, name, material participation, Part I amounts, and every stop question. A form stop completes the business without expense amounts. Otherwise the expense lines, line 7, line 28, and line 30 must be complete, and a loss needs the at-risk answer.

Fact.Name: A Schedule C business is missing a required header line
Fact.Description: False when the business list is unset or empty. True when a listed business has not finished lines A, B, D, E, F, H, and I (line C is the business name), or line J after line I is yes. An unanswered required header fact makes this fact true, so /scheduleCSectionIsComplete stays false and /flowIncomplete blocks submission. Nothing is invented for the PDF. Lines H, I, and J do not change net profit. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 4, PDF p. 5, and PDF p. 6. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 1, line J.

Fact.Name: Filer materially participates in this business
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 199A(i)(2)(B): "The term 'active qualified trade or business' means ... any qualified trade or business of the taxpayer in which the taxpayer materially participates (within the meaning of section 469(h))." 26 U.S.C. 469(h)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/469): material participation means involvement in the operations of the activity "on a basis which is (A) regular, (B) continuous, and (C) substantial." Used for Form 8995 line 16 (minimum deduction).

Fact.Name: Filer does not materially participate in this business
Schedule C businesses with material participation
Schedule C businesses without material participation
Schedule C expense line choices
Fact.Description: Part II lines this tool can deduct under 26 U.S.C. 162(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/162), plus Part V. Lines that need another form are separate yes/no stops, not choices.

Fact.Name: Returns and allowances
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 2. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 7, Line 2: report sales returns and allowances as a positive number. 26 U.S.C. 61.

Fact.Name: Other business income
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 6, ordinary other business income (scrap, recovered bad debts, interest on receivables). 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 7, Line 6. Fuel tax credits and Form 4797 recapture are a separate stop. 26 U.S.C. 61.

Fact.Name: Other business income is above zero
Fact.Description: True when line 6 is greater than zero, so the filer must say whether that income needs another form.

Fact.Name: Line 6 needs another form
Fact.Description: 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 7, Line 6: federal and state gasoline or fuel tax credit and recapture of a section 179 deduction or listed property (Form 4797) are included on line 6. This tool does not compute those. Yes stops the return.

Fact.Name: Gross receipts test amount for a small business taxpayer
Fact.Description: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §4.30, PDF p. 23 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf): "For taxable years beginning in 2026, a corporation or partnership meets the gross receipts test of § 448(c) for any taxable year if the average annual gross receipts of such entity for the 3-taxable-year period ending with the taxable year which precedes such taxable year does not exceed $32,000,000." 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 16: "You qualify as a small business taxpayer if you (a) have average annual gross receipts of $32 million or less for the 3 prior tax years (indexed for inflation), and (b) are not a tax shelter (as defined in section 448(d)(3))." 26 U.S.C. 448(c)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/448) states the 3-taxable-year test. The $25,000,000 statutory amount is adjusted by the revenue procedure. 26 U.S.C. 471(c)(1) and 263A(i)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/471, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/263A) use that test, and only for a taxpayer who is not a tax shelter prohibited from using the cash method under section 448(a)(3). 26 U.S.C. 471(c)(3) and 263A(i)(2) apply the test to an individual as if each trade or business were a corporation or partnership. The filer enters the 3-prior-year average. This fact is the amount that average is compared with. An average equal to $32,000,000 still meets the test ("does not exceed"). This year's Schedule C line 1 is not the test.

Fact.Name: Schedule C closing-inventory methods
Fact.Description: 2026 Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040sc.pdf, SHA-256 cc44e7d1150e54d991835814c1191f60a32617730ca9e50e6f532b51293a86b4), PDF p. 2, line 33: "Method(s) used to value closing inventory: a Cost, b Lower of cost or market, c Other (attach explanation)." 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 17, Line 33: "Your inventories can be valued at cost, the lower of cost or market, or any other method approved by the IRS." The fourth choice is the 26 U.S.C. 471(c)(1)(B)(i) method that does not keep an inventory (instructions, PDF p. 16).

Fact.Name: Inventory or cost of goods sold
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 4 and Part III. 26 U.S.C. 471(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/471): inventories are taken when necessary to clearly determine income. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i1040sc--dft.pdf), PDF p. 16, Cost of Goods Sold. No means this business does not complete Part III, and line 4 is zero. Yes asks for the line 33 method. Cost or lower of cost or market, with line 34 no, line 42 not below zero, line 35 equal to last year's closing inventory, a 3-prior-year average that does not exceed the Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §4.30 amount, and the filer not a tax shelter, is figured in Part III. Any other answer stops the return.

Fact.Name: Method used to value closing inventory
Fact.Description: Schedule C line 33, asked only when this business has inventory or cost of goods sold. Cost and lower of cost or market are the simple methods this tool figures. "Other" is line 33c and stops the return. Nonincidental materials and supplies is the 26 U.S.C. 471(c)(1)(B)(i) method of not keeping an inventory; claiming it while Part III is still required stops the return. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 16 and PDF p. 17.

Fact.Name: Line 33a, cost
Fact.Description: Closing inventory is valued at cost. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 33a.

Fact.Name: Line 33b, lower of cost or market
Fact.Description: Closing inventory is valued at the lower of cost or market. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2, line 33b.

Fact.Name: Line 33c, other
Fact.Description: Line 33c, "Other (attach explanation)." Not cost or lower of cost or market. Stops the return. 2026 Schedule C, PDF p. 2. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 17, Line 33.

Fact.Name: No-inventory method under section 471(c)
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 471(c)(1)(B)(i): the method "treats inventory as non-incidental materials and supplies." 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule C, PDF p. 16: "If you choose not to keep an inventory" and account for it as nonincidental materials and supplies, Part III is not completed. Choosing that method while this business still needs Part III is inconsistent and stops the return.

Fact.Name: Closing inventory uses cost or lower of cost or market
